subject: Bootstrapping to estimate variance in DSM

messages.author: 9dfffeb8a4f59233
messages.subject: Bootstrapping to estimate variance in DSM
parts:
Hi all

My second post to this forum. I've just set up a project using the DSM en=
gine of Distance 6. The project includes 10 repeat aerial surveys for wat=
erbirds over two adjoining survey areas, with a total of 853 transects be=
tween all the surveys. I segmented as small as I feasibly could given my =
strip width, so with 1km segments I have 16,952 segments. All the surveys=
were flown in winter over two years, so ideally I want to keep the data =
together so the DSM engine of Distance 6 gives me one mean estimate of de=
nsity for each species I filter out.

However, when it comes to bootstrapping for variance in Distance 6, extra=
polating from the progress indicator for 999 re-samples, I would need 12 =
days to run each set of bootstraps. I then split the data into the two su=
rvey areas as I figure it would be easy to combine the estimates geograph=
ically, but that still leaves me with several days of computer crunching.=


So my question is, is there a quicker way to run these bootstraps to esti=
mate variance? For example if I learn how to run it directly in R is this=
considerably quicker?

Ultimately I need to estimate density and variance in a portion of my sur=
vey area identified by a separate 'Region' shapefile, so unless there is =
a better way I need to estimate variance in each cell of my prediction gr=
id so I can sum these in my polygon of interest.

Any advice gratefully received...

Thanks

G.
